questions.q: Which shortcut inserts a brand-new worksheet in the workbook?
questions.solution: Shift+F11 adds a new worksheet. Ctrl+N creates a new workbook (file), and Ctrl+F11 has no default action in modern Excel.
questions.shortcut: New sheet inside the file = Shift+F11; whole new file = Ctrl+N.

questions.q: Which statement about SSDs and HDDs is correct?
options: SSDs use flash memory with no moving parts
HDDs are always faster than SSDs
questions.solution: An SSD stores data in NAND flash chips with no mechanical parts, making it faster and shock-resistant; an HDD stores data magnetically on spinning platters with a moving head, and is slower but cheaper per GB.
questions.shortcut: 'No moving parts' -> SSD, always. Any option giving moving parts to SSD or calling HDD faster is upside down.

questions.q: Which key combination switches between open application windows?
questions.solution: Alt+Tab cycles through all open windows. Ctrl+Tab switches tabs inside one application, Shift+Tab moves focus backwards, and Alt+F4 closes the window.
questions.shortcut: Alt = Active window: Alt+Tab switches it, Alt+F4 closes it.

questions.q: Encryption and data compression in the OSI model are the responsibility of the:
questions.solution: Presentation (layer 6) translates data formats and applies encryption/compression (JPEG, MP3, TLS concepts). Session manages dialogues, Transport moves segments.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The committee will announce the results.
options: The results will being announced by the committee.
The results would be announced by the committee.
The results will be announced by the committee.
The results will announced by the committee.
questions.solution: Simple future → **will be + V3**. B loses 'be'; C uses 'being' after a modal; D shifts the modal (would).

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The auditorium was ___ small ___ accommodate the entire graduating batch.
questions.solution: Adjective + bare verb after the second blank → the *too + adj + to + base verb* structure: **too small to accommodate**. 'So, that' would need a full clause ('so small that it could not accommodate'), 'very' forms no pair, and 'too, for' needs a noun after 'for'.
questions.shortcut: Recognise the skeleton: too + adj + to + verb.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The principal, as well as the teachers, / were present / at the annual function / held last Friday.
options: The principal, as well as the teachers,
questions.solution: With *as well as*, the verb agrees with the **first** subject, *The principal* (singular). So it should be **was present**.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The road is being repaired by the workers.
options: The workers is repairing the road.
The workers have repaired the road.
The workers are repairing the road.
The workers are repaired the road.
questions.solution: 'is being + V3' → present continuous: **are repairing** (plural subject). B writes V3 after are; C fails number; D changes tense to perfect.

questions.q: Minamata disease is caused by poisoning from:
questions.solution: **Minamata disease** (Japan, 1950s) was caused by **methylmercury** in industrial wastewater, which accumulated in fish. Cadmium caused itai-itai disease.

questions.q: Which mandala of the Rigveda is **entirely devoted to Soma**?
questions.solution: The **Ninth mandala** of the Rigveda is wholly addressed to **Soma** (the sacred drink/deity). Mandala III has the Gayatri Mantra, VII the Battle of Ten Kings, X the Purusha Sukta.
questions.shortcut: Anchors **3-7-9-10** → Gayatri, Ten Kings, **Soma**, Purusha Sukta.

questions.q: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from which rock?
questions.solution: Heat and pressure recrystallise **limestone** (calcium carbonate) into **marble**. Sandstone becomes quartzite, shale becomes slate and granite becomes gneiss.

questions.q: The Chinese pilgrim **Fa-Hien** visited India during the reign of —
questions.solution: **Fa-Hien (Faxian)** travelled in India c. 399–414 CE in the reign of **Chandragupta II Vikramaditya** and wrote *Fo-kwo-ki*. Hiuen Tsang came under Harsha (7th century).
questions.shortcut: F-H-I order: **F**a-Hien is the earliest → Gupta peak (Chandragupta II).

questions.q: Which of the following fractions is the largest?
The product of two numbers is 2028 and their HCF is 13. How many pairs of such numbers are possible?
questions.solution:
Let the numbers be $13a$ and $13b$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.
$13a \times 13b = 2028$ ⇒ $169ab = 2028$ ⇒ $ab = 12$.
Co-prime factor pairs of 12: $(1, 12)$ and $(3, 4)$.
Pairs of numbers: (13, 156) and (39, 52) ⇒ **2 pairs**.
questions.shortcut: product ÷ HCF² = 12 = 1×12 = 3×4 (co-prime only) ⇒ 2 pairs. (Answer 3 forgets the co-prime check: 2×6 shares a factor.)
questions.pattern: count pairs from product and HCF

questions.q: The perimeter of a rhombus is 40 cm and one of its diagonals is 12 cm. The area of the rhombus is:
questions.solution:
Side $=10$ cm. Half of the given diagonal $=6$, so the other half-diagonal $=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8$, giving
diagonals 12 and 16. Area $=\frac12\times12\times16=96$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: 6-8-10 triplet with the half-diagonals: other diagonal 16, area $\frac12\times12\times16=96$.

questions.q: If each edge of a cube increases by 10%, its volume increases by:
questions.solution: $(1.1)^3=1.331$, so the increase is 33.1%.
questions.shortcut: $1.1^3=1.331$. Trap: 21% is the surface increase; 30% treats volume as linear.

questions.q: **Suresh and Veena are siblings. Pooja is Suresh's daughter. Rohit is Veena's son.** How is **Rohit related to Pooja**?
questions.solution: Pooja and Rohit are children of siblings — they are **cousins**. (Nephew would need Rohit to be a child of Pooja's brother; uncle would need him to be a brother of Pooja's parent.)
questions.shortcut: Children of siblings = cousins, whatever the genders.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **ABCD : BDFH :: MNOP : ?**
questions.solution: A→B = +1, B→D = +2, C→F = +3, D→H = +4: the shifts themselves rise by 1. Apply (+1, +2, +3, +4) to MNOP: M+1=N, N+2=P, O+3=R, P+4=T → **NPRT**.
questions.shortcut: If constant shift fails, check whether the shift tuple itself is a series (+1,+2,+3,...) — the next most common rule.

questions.q: In a certain code, **CROWN is written as DTRAS**. How is **BLADE** written in that code?
questions.shortcut: Rising tuple — apply slot by slot; the W→A wrap is just (23+4)−26 = 1 = A.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **25, 49, 64, 81**
questions.solution: All are squares (5², 7², 8², 9²). 25, 49, 81 are squares of odd numbers; **64 = 8²** is the square of an even number → odd one out.
questions.shortcut: Level 1 squares, level 2 parity of roots — the standard two-level climb.
